Subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation

Hi Andrew,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Quick recap from our call and agreed next steps: 

Pain points (you shared):
- Frequent model timeouts during peak bidding windows (you reported 95th tail ~800ms vs target ~200ms).
- Single-region deployment has led to manual failovers and elevated error rates during infra incidents.
- No formal graceful-degradation policy: when GPUs/hosts drop, traffic often retries and compounds latency.

Current stack (as I captured it):
- In-house inference for ranking (~100+ qps per model shard) running on AWS EKS + p3 instances.
- Redis for prefix/KV cache, custom autoscaler for pods.
- No consistent multi-region routing — primary in us-west.

Success criteria you called out:
- 95th percentile inference latency <= 250ms at sustained 500 qps.
- Overall request success > 99.5% during incidents (graceful degradation targets).
- Ability to failover to a compatible, lower-cost/quantized model with <200ms additional latency impact.

Incident history we reviewed:
- 2026-03-12: AZ-level networking issue in us-west — manual failover; ~30% request errors for ~45 minutes.
- 2026-07-02: Autoscaler flapping during peak; degraded tail latency and elevated timeouts for ~20 minutes.

Fallback and mitigation options we discussed:
- Multi-region routing with active primary (us-west) and warm standby (us-east).
- Automatic fallback to an 8-bit quantized model family for heavy load or degraded nodes.
- Prefix/KV caching for high-repeat traffic to reduce work on model servers.
- Canary and progressive rollouts to validate fallbacks without impacting traffic.

SLO / SLA notes:
- You mentioned a target SLO of 99.9% availability and a desire for a 100ms p50 improvement during peak.
- Redwood can offer SLA-backed targets on Dedicated with negotiated service credits; we'll surface typical latency/availability profiles for the proposed config.

Next steps (agreed):
1) I will share a short SOC2 summary and a Mutual Action Plan (attached) for your procurement/security review.
2) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with your infra/engineering team next week — Marissa will lead the session from our side.
3) Redwood to produce an initial cost + latency projection for a Dedicated pool with multi-region failover and fallback model options by EOD Friday.
4) If the projection looks good, we'll follow with a Proof-of-Concept plan and a mutual-action timeline for procurement and pilot.

Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf, Mutual_Action_Plan_ACME.docx

Thanks,
Ben

Redwood Inference
